strengths: Three clearly distinct stances: beauty, the indifferent void, and connection.
Turn 7 turns the debate into a concrete, low-cost reading test.
Section E gives branching conditions tied to the reader's preference.
weaknesses: Its recommendations do not fit the request: Howards End is long, and Daisy Miller ends in death (Section E, turn 7).
Turn 6 misattributes Sartre's condemned to freedom to the Absurdist.
Form breach: turn 7 leans on Henry James, who is not one of the three minds.
editorNotes: Require recommended books to match the user's stated constraints (length, mood) and flag known mismatches.
Forbid a turn from citing any author or book outside its mind's assigned source.
Require at least one explicit concession or revision by a named mind.
Make rebuttals quote or paraphrase the opponent's actual prior words, not stock phrases.
